title: 📰 AI news · October 19
takeaway: Today is about access: a home router with a flaw in its Wi-Fi chip opens the door to your network, and your project keys often live behind it. Recommendation: find your router model, check whether updates still come out for it, and move project keys out of open files.

items.title: A 2010 flaw found in Broadcom Wi-Fi chips
items.text: A researcher found a flaw in Broadcom Wi-Fi chips: someone within range can run their own code on the router without a password. In Belgium alone, over 1.5 million provider routers are exposed, with no updates as of October 15. If your projects run from a home network, the router guards the door to your keys. Find your router model and check whether updates are still released for it.

items.title: Anthropic puts 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund
items.text: The fund will work on projects for the public good: donations and direct payments to groups of people. For every 50% rise in company value, 2% more shares may be added. Details are promised in the coming months.

items.title: Three aurora models flashed in the OpenAI API
items.text: Red, green and blue appeared in the API and vanished, then showed up in blind image tests on Arena. The community thinks it is GPT-Image-3. OpenAI has confirmed nothing.
